subject: Hosted evaluation — access patterns, endpoints, and rate caps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finlytics.com>, Alan Murphy <alan.murphy@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted evaluation — access patterns, endpoints, and rate caps

Hi Laura / Alan —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed set of next steps so we can scope whether Hosted API covers FinLytics' needs or if Dedicated/Private will be required.

Key notes from the demo / discovery:
- Primary workload: real-time document classification + extraction for compliance pipelines; 95th percentile latency requirement ~300ms per request.
- Traffic profile: steady ~8 qps with burst capacity up to ~40 qps for trading windows.
- Data controls: request/response data cannot persist beyond 30 days in customer storage; audit logs required for any troubleshooting.
- SSO and SCIM: your infra team prefers SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for role mapping.

Initial assessment (Hosted API):
- Pros: fastest onboarding, streaming endpoints for long outputs, transparent per-token billing.
- Constraints to verify: whether automatic prefix caching and continuous batching will keep tail latency within 300ms during 40 qps bursts; hosted retention policy aligns with your 30-day requirement and audit log access.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a short Hosted quickstart pack (redwood-hosted-quickstart-guide.pdf) and a sample traffic CSV — please share a representative 24-hour traffic dump if comfortable.
2) Can your infra lead (Alan) confirm SSO vendor and whether IP allowlist is required for API access? If IP allowlist is needed, that pushes toward Dedicated or Private without additional networking work.
3) We can run a 2-week hosted pilot with rate caps configured to mirror your peaks; I recommend starting with endpoints behind a single API key and enabling prefix caching.

Timing: if you can share the traffic sample by EOD Friday (Oct 16), we’ll scope a pilot plan and share a test configuration by Oct 19.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: (555) 322-1187
redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-guide.pdf (guide, 6 pages); finlytics-sample-traffic.csv (CSV, 24h sample); sso-integration-specs.docx (SSO fields)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Murphy <alan.murphy@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:01:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation — access patterns, endpoints, and rate caps

Thanks Vivek — helpful recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

- We'll extract a 24-hour traffic sample and drop it into the shared Drive link you sent by Friday.
- SSO: Okta (SAML) + we use SCIM for provisioning. IP allowlist is not currently enabled for outbound API calls, but we do require requests to originate from our VPC NAT IPs — happy to share those.
- Data retention: 30 days is a hard requirement for persisted copies; ephemeral caching for inference is OK if it can be configured not to be logged. We also need structured audit logs for any admin actions.

On latency — the 300ms 95th requirement is aggressive for larger extraction prompts. Would you be able to run a short test with the same model family and the caching profile you recommend? That will tell us if Hosted can meet the SLO or whether Dedicated makes sense.

I'll loop in Alan to confirm the NAT IPs.

Laura Chen
Head of Platform | FinLytics
laura.chen@finlytics.com

Vivek / team —

We can provide the NAT IPs (two addresses) and the Okta SAML metadata. We typically prefer vendor APIs to be restricted to our egress IPs for governance, so if Hosted requires a broad public reachability that would complicate things — please call that out in the pilot config.

Also: two clarifications from infra:
- Audit logs: must include request id, API key, timestamp, and masked response hashes.
- Retention: 30 days in customer-managed storage; if Hosted keeps temporary logs, we need a deletion policy enforced via SLA.

If Hosted can pass these controls and demonstrate latency under load, we can proceed with the pilot. Otherwise we'll look at Dedicated with a reserved pool.

—Alan

Thanks Alan / Laura —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick responses and a concrete pilot plan: 

1) Pilot config we will propose by Monday (Oct 19):
   - Hosted endpoints configured with a dedicated API key for FinLytics, explicit prefix caching enabled, and continuous batching tuned to favor low-latency (we'll share the batching target).
   - Rate caps: base 10 qps with burst allowance to 45 qps during trading window windows; we will instrument 95th/99th latency in the dashboard.
   - Data controls: provide an SLA clause for 30-day deletion for any persisted artefacts + exportable admin audit logs (request id, API key, timestamp, masked response hash).
   - Network controls: we can accept calls from your NAT IPs and add a note on recommended IP allowlist behavior; some features (edge caching) rely on public endpoints — we'll call out tradeoffs.

2) Quick validation step: as soon as you drop the traffic sample, our infra team (Marissa) will run a synthetic replay on the proposed caching/batching profile and share a latency distribution within 48 hours.

3) Decision gate: if the 95th latency under replay meets < 300ms we proceed with a 2-week hosted pilot. If not, we'll scope Dedicated capacity with a reserved pool and private networking.

I'll attach the pilot checklist and a proposed SLA excerpt in my follow-up (will include DocuSign link if you want the SLA redline-ready).

Thanks — talk soon.
Vivek
